summary.name: Evolution or Rebellion? The rise of Site Reliability Engineers (SRE)
summary.one_liner: A 2016 blog post by Rob Hirschfeld on the rise of Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) as a job role, how it differs from traditional operations, and its links to DevOps.
use_cases: Understanding what a Google-style SRE role is
Reading the debate on DevOps versus SRE
Finding context on the developer and ops tension
Learning why companies move infrastructure to outsourced providers
Finding pointers to SRE podcasts and write-ups
summary.what_it_does: The post is an opinion essay about Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) as a job classification popularized by Google. It argues that SRE is about operational excellence and automating infrastructure rather than administration, and that it is not tied to any specific infrastructure. It describes a tension between developers and operations, and a trend of enterprises shifting from internal IT to outsourced infrastructure such as Amazon's services. The author sees containers and serverless as a sign that developers want to avoid ops work. The page links to other SRE resources, including a Datanauts podcast episode and write-ups by Susan Fowler and Patrick Hill.
notable: Frames SRE as a recognized engineering role, popularized by Google, that builds and automates infrastructure
Links to podcasts and reviews on SRE, including Charity Majors on Datanauts #65 and Susan Fowler on no-ops tensions
Reflects on the author's years of writing about operations under names like DevOps and Ready State
caveats: Opinion piece from 2016; it does not give a tutorial or tool documentation
Page is a short essay with no product, pricing, or platform details
